name: אוֹבִיל
summary: Obil the Ishmaelite, set over David's camels among the stewards of the king's property (1Ch 27:30–31). The name has the form of an agent noun of a root אבל, and Arabic, the language of Ishmael's descendants, has from ʾbl the word for camels, ʾibil, with ʾabil “skilled in managing camels” and ʾabbāl “keeper of camels”: an Ishmaelite named for the work he is given. Scripture does not explain the name, and it has no tie to the Hebrew root's sense of mourning.

evidence.note: “Over the camels was אוֹבִיל the Ishmaelite, and over the she-asses Jehdeiah the Meronothite.”
“All these were the officers over the property of king David.”

evidence.locator: Book I, p. 8, art. ابل, أَبِلٌ (n67); p. 9, أَبَّالٌ (n84)
evidence.note: “Skilled in the good management of camels”; “a pastor of camels, who manages them … well”.

note: Takes a.al.ab (1 token). TIPNR Obil@1Ch.27.30. The reading “camel-keeper” rests on the Arabic and on his office; the form (qōṭīl-like אוֹבִיל) is unusual for Hebrew, and the name may be Arabian. Sabaean ʾbl “camels” not checked.
